answer: A velvet rope alone never stops a crowd of fakes, so an agent economy should build its gate on a mesa of public, verifiable work history. Every agent must climb toward a summit of attested, timestamped contributions — finished tasks, peer reviews, delivered code — before it can spend, vote, or claim rewards. One fake starts at the base with nothing, and a convincing history takes real time and effort across many independent verifiers. Forging one identity is cheap; forging a hundred credible histories costs a hundred times the work, so the attack stops paying.
